# 2. Take Apart the Ender 3

The Ender 3 gives you the extrusion, stepper motors, belts, pulleys, rollers and most of the
hardware. You won't reuse its control board or screen.

1. Unplug the printer and disconnect the power supply.
2. Remove the top bar, then the Z lead screw and Z motor.
3. Remove the two bolts at the front of the base to reach the control board, and the two bolts
   holding the screen.
4. Unbolt the extrusions from each other.
5. Keep: extrusion, stepper motors, belts, pulleys, rollers, the fan, and every bolt and T-nut.
   Factory holes in the extrusion can be ignored.

!!! warning
    Be careful with ribbon cables and don't yank wires out of connectors: you will reuse the motor
    cables.

!!! tip
    Bag and label the hardware as it comes off (M3, M4, M5 by length). It saves a lot of time
    later.
